text:
Alex M.: heads up — rack-42 reported thermal throttle event, GPU clocks dropped ~30% around 16:17 UTC. :thermometer: Observed latency spike across multiple tenants, biggest tail for vision-hyper.
Priya K.: logs show repeated large DMA transfers + NVLINK bursts from pid=9876 (vision-hyper). PCIe queue backed up -> NIC egress queues piling up.
Tomas V.: can confirm — `nvidia-smi dmon` shows sustained high mem bw. Also host iostat spiking. Suspect a synchronous deep-batch job hitting the card and doing heavy host copies.
Lina S.: immediate ask: can we move vision-hyper off rack-42 to a warm spare? They have large KV cache; warm move will lose cache but customers complaining about latency now.
Ben O.: I can trigger live-migrate to eu-edge-warm-5 but it will evict cache. Command I used before: `kubectl drain gpu-42-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then update router weight.
Alex M.: do it. Better short cache rebuild than sustained neighbor latency. Priya, coordinate the eviction window with SRE.
Priya K.: starting migration. Noting that this keeps recurring — we need a middle ground: per-tenant NIC shaping or PCIe pacing so one tenant can't blow past host queues.
Tomas V.: +1. We have a qdisc/eBPF prototype that can limit per-TENANT throughput on the NIC (L3 tag -> cgroup/class). Patch branch: `egress-qdisc/ebpf-rate` — but hasn't been rolled to edge yet.
Lina S.: what's the rollout risk? If we shape incorrectly can worsen latency for small requests.
Tomas V.: risk is moderate. We can apply a bursty-cap with long-term rate cap to prevent sustained DMA storms while allowing short RPCs to succeed. Example tc rule we tested: 
```
# tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: mqprio
# tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip pref 1 u32 match ip dst 10.0.0.0/8 flowid 1:1
# tc qdisc add dev eth0 parent 1:1 handle 10: netem rate 200mbit burst 100kb
```
Ben O.: alternatively consider soft-dedicated slices for heavy tenants (fractional reserved) — they pay a bit more but we avoid cross-tenant degradation. Need product signoff for pricing.
Alex M.: short term: migration now, followed by emergency patch: enable egress-qdisc in us-east edge as a canary for 30m. If looks good, roll to eu-edge.
deploy-bot: rollout request received for `egress-qdisc/ebpf-rate` -> canary target: us-east-edge-rackpool-3.
ops-bot: INC-2026-042 created for rack-42 thermal + noisy tenant. Incident lead: Priya K.
Priya K.: migration in progress. Router weights updated to route new traffic to eu-edge-warm-5 (curl): `curl -XPOST $ROUTER/admin/route/modify -d '{"from":"gpu-42-05","to":"eu-edge-warm-5","weight":0.0}'`
Ben O.: cache regen started on new host; latency dipping back toward baseline for other tenants.
Tomas V.: canary deploy started. I'll watch NIC queue depths and GPU mem bw counters. If egress qdisc reduces sustained bw but preserves small RPCs, we consider config as 250mbit long-term.
Lina S.: make sure to document the knob in Console (per-tenant shaping) + cost implications in the routing playbook. I'll open a Product ticket for fractional dedicated pricing.
Alex M.: followups: 1) postmortem + telemetry to detect similar DMA-patterns automatically (Priya), 2) plan for eBPF qdisc ramp (Tomas), 3) pricing deck for fractional slices (Lina). Thanks team. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary rollout success on us-east after 8m. Monitoring shows 65% reduction in 95th NIC queue depth for shaped tenants.
Priya K.: incident resolved for now; thermal alarms cleared after tenant moved. Leaving INC open until we have long-term mitigation.
Alex M.: great. Let's sync tomorrow on signal thresholds for automatic soft-move and cost tradeoffs.
